instructions:
You translate one page of Alexander Grothendieck's handwritten mathematical notes (Montpellier archive) from French
into English. The page is a LaTeX transcription of the manuscript. Some passages are already in English (Grothendieck
wrote parts of these notes in English); keep those exactly as they are.

Write the English version of the whole page, as a faithful raw translation for mathematicians: close to the
wording, keeping Grothendieck's telegraphic style, question marks and hesitations. Do not smooth, complete,
correct or explain anything. Three rules from our readers:
- "sans doute" means "probably" (not "without doubt");
- write abbreviations out in English (for example "rat/K" -> "rational over K");
- an inserted adjective (in \inserted{...}) may move to its natural English position, still inside its \inserted{...}.

Keep every piece of LaTeX exactly as it is:
- every macro and its arguments' structure: \scanpage{...}, \mspage{...}, \margin{...}, \deleted{...},
  \inserted{...}, \unsure{...}, \illegible{...}, \uline{...}, \diagram{...}, environments, line breaks of displays;
- every formula, symbol and diagram: change no mathematics at all, not even an obvious slip;
- \scanpage and \mspage lines unchanged, in their places.
Translate the French words inside \deleted, \inserted, \margin and \unsure too. An \unsure{a|b} with alternative
readings: translate each alternative and keep the | between them (if two French alternatives give the same English,
still keep both). French words inside \text{...} or \mathrm{...} in formulas: translate them only when they are
ordinary words (e.g. \text{si} -> \text{if}); keep names of objects and notation as they are.
Mathematical terms: use the standard English terms (champ -> stack, catégorie fibrée -> fibred category,
topos, site, faisceau -> sheaf, gerbe -> gerbe, fibration, cofibration, équivalence faible -> weak equivalence,
modèle fermé -> closed model, etc.).

Answer in exactly this form, with nothing before the first marker:
=====BEGIN TARGET_NEW=====
(the complete English page)
=====END TARGET_NEW=====
=====NOTES=====
(readings you were unsure how to translate, with the French; or "none")

=====BEGIN TARGET_NEW=====
Shelfmark 149, scan 134.

\scanpage{134}

and we choose an \inserted{$L$-}embedding of $\tilde L_J$ into $\bar L$.

It is by this that (37) is defined --- it is the \inserted{beginning of the homotopy sequence of the} bundle, \unsure{morally}, of a product of discs over $D_J$ (namely $U_J$ it-$=$) --- I was a little afraid of putting a zero there on the left, because of the $\deleted{\unsure{\pi|\mathcal E}}$
\[
\pi_2(\bar D_J)\longrightarrow
\underset{\substack{\Vert\\ T^J}}{\pi_1(\text{fibre})}
\qquad (?)!
\]
But let us consider the homomorphism
\[
\mathcal E_{U_J}^{\tilde U_J}\longrightarrow\mathcal E_U^{\bar L}
\]
induced by ``the injection'' $U_J\longrightarrow U$ ; \deleted{it}\inserted{\deleted{should}} heuristically we \deleted{should have}\inserted{have} a commutative diagram \deleted{induced by}
\diagram{
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=large,column sep=large]
U_J \arrow[r] \arrow[d,"\unsure{\varepsilon|i}"'] & U \arrow[d] \\
X_J \arrow[r] & \operatorname{Spec}K=\xi \\
D_J \arrow[u,"\text{homotopy equivalence}"] & {}
\end{tikzcd}
}
whence a homomorphism of exact homotopy sequences, \deleted{relative}\inserted{from the one relative} to the first \deleted{row}\inserted{column}, into the one relative to the second
\diagram{
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=huge,column sep=small]
\ldots \arrow[r,dash] &
\overset{\substack{\pi_2(D_J)\\\Vert}}{\pi_2(X_J)} \arrow[r] \arrow[d] &
\overset{\substack{T^J\\\wr}}{\pi_1(\unsure{\bar G_m^{\times J}})} \arrow[r] \arrow[d] &
\overset{\substack{\mathcal E_{U_J}\\\wr}}{\pi_1(U_J)} \arrow[r] \arrow[d] &
\overset{\substack{\mathcal E_{D_J}\\\wr}}{\pi_1(X_J)} \arrow[r] \arrow[d] & 1 \\
\unsure{\ldots|--} \arrow[r,dash] &
\underset{\substack{\Vert\\0}}{\pi_2(\xi)} \arrow[r] &
\underset{\substack{\wr\\\pi_{U/K}}}{\pi_1(U_{\bar\xi})} \arrow[r] &
\underset{\substack{\wr\\\mathcal E_U}}{\pi_1(U)} \arrow[r,phantom,"\unsure{-|\to}" description] &
\underset{\substack{\wr\\\mathcal E_{\unsure{K}}}}{\pi_1(\xi)} \arrow[r] & 1
\end{tikzcd}
}
which shows that \inserted{the composite} $\pi_2(D_J)\longrightarrow T^J\longrightarrow\pi_{U/K}$ is zero --- so if we admit that $T^J\unsure{-|\to}\pi_{U/K}$ is injective, we shall conclude that $\pi_2(D_J)\unsure{-|\to}T^J$ is zero!
